study type: Modified Delphi process and systematic review
exposure: Prior history of Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS)
Placenta previa with cervical involvement (ultrasound feature)
outcome: Prenatal evaluation of Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS)
Surgical outcome in patients with high probability of PAS at delivery
cohort: An international panel of 31 obstetric ultrasound imaging experts participated in a three-round Delphi consensus-building process, following a systematic review of 15 articles describing ultrasound signs for Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS).
finding: The study confirmed the continued importance of seven established standardized ultrasound signs for Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) in high-risk patients and routine mid-gestation scans, and identified specific patient histories and ultrasound features that increase the probability of PAS.
mod_finding: A prior history of at least one Cesarean delivery was identified as an indication for detailed PAS ultrasound assessment, linking a mode of birth to the need for specific prenatal evaluation.
cross-section timing: Prenatal evaluation, specifically during routine mid-gestation scans
